nodes.rationale: Pydantic schemas and api/types.ts align authenticated JSON APIs, WebSocket data and RabbitMQ messages.

nodes.label: Temporary inventory holds
nodes.rationale: Reservations expire and must be rechecked before confirmation; DB row locks prevent double allocation.

nodes.label: Validated idempotent messaging
nodes.rationale: Consumers validate schemas, remember message IDs, retry, dead-letter and write message history.

nodes.label: Mock route registry
nodes.rationale: Page mocks register handlers; VITE_USE_MOCKS serves the desktop without the backend.

nodes.label: Shared backend helpers
nodes.rationale: Settings, DB sessions, role guards, audit, messaging and AI client are reused by each domain.

nodes.label: Theme token vocabulary

nodes.label: Typed desktop API client
nodes.rationale: apiFetch, api/types.ts and useLiveEvents provide shared REST and WebSocket access.

nodes.label: Approval pack
nodes.rationale: The manager sees the PO, extraction, quotation comparison, material availability, plan options, impact Gantt and reply draft.

nodes.label: Code computes business facts
nodes.rationale: LLMs read and explain; quantities, capacity, costs and dates come from code.

nodes.label: Hub-and-spoke architecture
nodes.rationale: Only the orchestrator sends tasks to agents and receives their results; agents do not coordinate directly.

nodes.label: Human-sent customer email
nodes.rationale: The Order agent drafts messages; sales sends outside the system.

nodes.label: Isometric Factory floor
nodes.rationale: Machine beacons, face displays, motion, cart paths and machine inspection report live production.

nodes.label: Live Agent map
nodes.rationale: Stations and RabbitMQ tracks animate task/result/event traffic and support message inspection and order replay.

nodes.label: Motion accessibility
nodes.rationale: Reduced motion and page visibility must gate animation.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL source of truth
nodes.rationale: Clients hold no local business data; workflows recover from durable database state.

nodes.label: Read-only orchestrator chat
nodes.rationale: Chat tools inspect data and run what-if calculations, without approving, reserving or sending.

nodes.label: UTC storage with local display
nodes.rationale: All times are stored in UTC and presented in APP_TIMEZONE.

nodes.label: Electron React desktop
nodes.rationale: The shared desktop client shows factory floor, agent map, approvals, dashboards and history.

nodes.label: FastAPI manufacturing backend
nodes.rationale: Python services coordinate PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ and CP-SAT scheduling.

nodes.label: Repository team ownership
nodes.rationale: P1 owns foundation and integration; P2 domain agents; P3 orchestration; P4 desktop; P5 isometric figures.

nodes.label: Single manager approval
nodes.rationale: PO extraction, inventory checking and planning culminate in a single informed manager decision.

nodes.label: Loopback-only infrastructure ports
nodes.rationale: Bind database, queue and mail ports to 127.0.0.1 so other network hosts cannot reach them.

nodes.label: RabbitMQ port-connectivity readiness
nodes.rationale: RabbitMQ ping succeeds before AMQP accepts connections; checking port connectivity prevents agents starting too early.

nodes.label: Floor-layout Alembic migration 0003
nodes.description: Adds floor_layout, floor_placements and nullable machines.original_floor_x/original_floor_y. Archives coordinates before snapping to 10 units; half-cells round toward positive infinity. Retains machine UUIDs and production references.

nodes.label: Floor layout PostgreSQL acceptance checks
nodes.description: Covers migrations, permissions, validation, concurrent first saves, retained records, and an injected post-flush failure verifying full rollback.
nodes.rationale: TEST_DATABASE_URL must name a disposable database because the test fixture recreates it.

nodes.label: Editable wall runs
nodes.description: Horizontal or vertical wall runs have editable length and count as one undo step.

nodes.label: Undo and redo history
nodes.description: Includes additions, moves, rotations, removals, property edits and resizing. One drag or wall run is one history step; text edits commit on blur.

nodes.label: Floor and machine API compatibility
nodes.description: Old machine POST/PATCH writes return explanatory 409. GET /floor includes typed layout, rotation and placed machines. GET /machines preserves the full production registry; floor_x/floor_y remain world coordinates synchronized on saves.

nodes.label: Validated floor resizing
nodes.description: Resize dimensions are entered in cells; clipping any placed item, including exterior fixtures, blocks resize.

nodes.label: Floor editor browser acceptance checks
nodes.description: Runs against an isolated mock preview; covers roles, placement, history, save/cancel, clipping and unsaved-change warnings. Mock state is in memory; reload persistence requires the real backend.

nodes.label: Floor-edit draft lifecycle
nodes.description: Save retains history; undo after Save becomes unsaved. Cancel restores the latest successful save and clears history. Background refresh and reconnect preserve draft and history; leaving warns on unsaved changes.

nodes.label: Saved floor decor catalog
nodes.description: Structure, furniture and markings reuse Anatomy geometry and theme materials. Deck and expansion joints derive from floor dimensions; machine bays follow rotated footprints.

nodes.label: Admin-only layout editing
nodes.rationale: Non-admin roles keep the live view; server-side layout writes deny non-admin roles with 403. Settings links admins directly to the editor.

nodes.label: Derived initial floor layout
nodes.rationale: Before the first Save, GET derives placements and initial decor without writing. Bounds include exterior fixtures and negative coordinates; legacy collisions require user correction rather than deleting or silently moving machines. After Save, deleted decor stays deleted.

nodes.label: Separate machine identity and floor placement
nodes.norm_label: separate machine identity and floor placement
nodes.rationale: Removing a placement retains production records, events, jobs and planning availability; unplaced machines can be placed again. Decor never contributes to machine registry counts or live status.

nodes.label: Saved-layout rollback preservation
nodes.rationale: Application rollback can leave additive schema intact. Schema downgrade restores archived coordinates only before any layout is saved and refuses to drop saved layouts; export and reconcile before separately planned destructive rollback.

nodes.label: Transactional revision-checked layout save
nodes.rationale: One PostgreSQL transaction commits dimensions, decor, placements and machine properties. Advisory locks, revision checks, validation and audit records prevent inconsistent reads and silent concurrent overwrites; live machine status is not overwritten.

nodes.label: Durable order state machine
nodes.rationale: Persisted next action, task identity, deadlines and retries support restart recovery.

nodes.label: QC completion gate
nodes.rationale: All production counts and latest required checks must pass before close_order succeeds.

nodes.label: Role-filtered WebSockets
nodes.rationale: Store users get metadata without payloads/cost; notifications target listed recipients only.

nodes.label: Serialized approval decisions
nodes.rationale: Order row locks serialize concurrent decisions and result applications; only the current attempt may advance a workflow.

nodes.label: Timezone-aware KPI calculations
nodes.rationale: Reporting uses APP_TIMEZONE, effective date ranges, actual durations and logged AI costs.

nodes.label: Back-dated recovery records
nodes.rationale: Enter paper slips oldest first, preserve references, reconcile stock and replan affected work.

nodes.label: Backup and restore procedure
nodes.rationale: Hourly pg_dump plus document-volume backup supports recovery; production should use point-in-time restore.

nodes.label: Grafilab AI configuration
nodes.rationale: OpenAI-compatible provider and per-agent models are configured through environment settings.

nodes.label: Paper fallback
nodes.rationale: Store slips, order sheets, machine sheets and QC sheets keep factory work moving during outages.

nodes.label: P5 browser verification and performance
nodes.description: Mock captures cover desktop, phone and 4x details with WebGL disabled. Line checker found zero floating endpoints across 18 floor and 12 map endpoints in both themes. Five-message/sec Chrome probes averaged 72 fps alone and 17 fps alongside capture; steady 60 fps on target laptop remains unconfirmed.

nodes.label: Dashboards and chart table views
nodes.rationale: Seven charts and KPI tiles use a common date range; every chart offers a data table.

nodes.label: Global chat notifications and refresh
nodes.rationale: Chat streams with tool chips; notifications show toast/native alerts; live events invalidate affected queries.

nodes.label: Keyboard and reduced-motion support
nodes.rationale: Enter opens rows; Escape closes dialogs and drawers; loading pulses stop under reduced motion.

nodes.label: Role-filtered navigation
nodes.rationale: Admin can open every page; manager, sales, planner, store and QC receive their assigned pages and controls.

nodes.label: Shared UI building blocks
nodes.rationale: DataTable, QueryState, dialogs, drawers, MiniGantt, StatusBadge, KpiTile, Money and PageHeader are shared across sections.

nodes.label: SVG animation frame gating
nodes.rationale: Animations update SVG attributes, and visibility/intersection observers gate the frame loop without React renders on every frame. Tests cover hidden tabs and reduced motion.

nodes.label: Live isometric factory floor
nodes.description: Bays use floor_x/floor_y; cutaways show machine internals, beacons show status, panels show order and part count, and the office monitor shows pending approvals.

nodes.label: Floor snapshots and event refresh
nodes.description: GET /floor supplies snapshots; machine status events update beacons immediately and refresh floor/overview, while order and approval events refresh the summary.

nodes.label: Machine readouts and operations drawers
nodes.description: Hover/focus shows readouts; click/Enter opens jobs, utilisation, events and maintenance. Manager, planner and admin see status/breakdown forms using the operations API.

nodes.label: Transient delivery cart
nodes.description: Live animation outside the saved decor catalog.

nodes.label: P5 integration requests reference
nodes.description: Outstanding backend integration details for P5, which starts from P1 foundation; browser checks use mocks.

nodes.label: Material-result delivery cart assignment
nodes.rationale: The cart leaves the store only when a successful Material result explicitly identifies both issue and destination; ambiguous or missing assignments leave it parked.

links.description: The live Material-result cart behavior corresponds to the transient delivery animation excluded from editor saves.
